# rhun

> rhun is a small, very fast code editor for Linux (x86-64), macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (x64), written in assembly. It has tabs, a file explorer, syntax highlighting for 127 languages and file formats, find and replace, a built-in terminal, Git history and diffs, fuzzy search, an optional Vim mode, 40 color themes and an agents panel that shows Claude Code and Codex sessions live. Free and open source (MIT). Current version: @VERSION@.

Facts:

- One static binary under 700 KB on Linux (fonts, themes and grammars included), with no libc, toolkit or runtime. It draws every pixel itself and speaks Wayland and X11 directly; on macOS the same source is translated to native Apple silicon code and runs in an AppKit window. Windows uses an assembly Win32 adapter and ConPTY.
- Install on Linux and macOS: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/vshvedov/rhun/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` (or `wget -qO-`). No root; checks SHA-256 checksums and, on macOS, the developer signature. Uninstall: add `sh -s -- --uninstall`.
- Updates: rhun checks GitHub once a day in the background; the status bar offers a new version, installs it and restarts into it on Windows, Linux and macOS. Windows stages a checksum-verified release and installs it after the editor exits for restart; writable ZIP installations also update in place.
- Settings: `~/.config/rhun/config`, applied while running. Grammars: `~/.config/rhun/syntax/NAME.syn`. Themes: `~/.config/rhun/themes/NAME.theme`.
- Windows: Windows 10 version 1809 or later, x64. Extract the Windows ZIP and open rhun.exe, or use the one-command PowerShell installer shown on the website. No package manager is required. Settings are in %APPDATA%\rhun, sessions in %LOCALAPPDATA%\rhun. Native ARM64, code signing and the Unix control socket are not included.

## Docs

- [Docs](https://rhun.app/docs/): short guides to getting started, editing, the terminal, agents, Git, and customization
- [Full guide](https://rhun.app/guide.md): features, install and update, usage, shortcuts, configuration, grammars and themes
- [README](https://github.com/vshvedov/rhun/blob/main/README.md): overview

## Extensions

- [Extensions guide](https://rhun.app/docs/extensions/): installing from GitHub, what extensions can do, writing your own
- [Protocol v1](https://rhun.app/extensions/v1/v1.md): the whole extension protocol as Markdown, written for coding agents; [grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhun-editor/extension-protocol/main/v1/v1.abnf) and [manifest schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhun-editor/extension-protocol/main/v1/v1.json)
- [Rust template](https://github.com/rhun-editor/template-rust), [Go template](https://github.com/rhun-editor/template-go), [C/C++ header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhun-editor/extension-protocol/main/c/rhunext.h): start here; each template has AGENTS.md
- [Skills](https://github.com/rhun-editor/skills): a Claude Code and Codex plugin for writing, testing and releasing extensions
- Extensions are native programs (Rust preferred, Go, C, C++) talking to rhun over stdin/stdout, one line per message; they can add commands, edit documents, mark diagnostics, answer hover, draw charts and pictures in tabs (views), and provide completion, signature help, go to definition, references, document symbols, code actions, rename and format (workspace edits checked whole before applying). Test with `rhun-ext-check` and `rhun --headless --script`.

## Get it

- [Installer](https://github.com/vshvedov/rhun/releases/latest/download/install.sh): the one-command install script for Linux and macOS
- [Releases](https://github.com/vshvedov/rhun/releases): archives for Linux x86-64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64, with SHA-256 checksums
